title: The five quarters that built the rally
body:
The stock spent most of 2023 and 2024 trading below SEK 5. Then, in the eighteen months that followed the arrival of a new chief executive, it ran to SEK 72.90 — a 40-fold move from its five-year floor of SEK 1.80, placing a market capitalisation of roughly SEK 22.7 billion (approximately $2.2 billion) on a company that lost SEK 178 million on SEK 307 million of revenue in its most recent fiscal year. The move demands explanation. Five quarters supply most of it.

## August 2024: The handover

The starting gun was quiet. On 19 August 2024, Sivers announced that Anders Storm was stepping down and that Vickram Vathulya — with a background in optical networking and photonics commercialisation — would take the helm. Vathulya did not immediately change the financial trajectory. FY2024 results, as originally reported under Swedish K3 accounting standards, showed net sales of SEK 243.7 million and a net loss of SEK 116.3 million. But he signalled a sharper commercial focus on co-packaged optics, repositioning the photonics narrative away from generic "laser supplier" framing and toward a specific upstream slot in the AI datacenter supply chain. The language in investor materials shifted; so did the pipeline composition.

## H1 2025: Rights issue and the quiet build

The first half of 2025 brought necessary but dilutive housekeeping. A SEK 95 million rights issue — roughly 8% dilution — kept the balance sheet viable while Vathulya reshaped the commercial book. The broader capital context was sobering: shares outstanding have more than doubled since 2020, a 101% dilution that reflects the cost of surviving a decade-long pre-profitability growth phase. Free cash outflow, which had reached SEK 151 million as recently as 2022, compressed to SEK 66 million by year-end 2025 — real improvement, though the company ended the year with only SEK 43.5 million of cash on hand.

The wireless segment — mmWave beamformers for satellite communications customers including the European Space Agency and Intelsat — continued to carry product revenue. But investor attention was migrating toward photonics, and toward what Sivers could mean for co-packaged optics specifically.

## September 29, 2025: The POET anchor

The inflection moment arrived at the end of the third quarter. On 29 September 2025, Sivers and [POET Technologies](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market) announced a strategic collaboration to build External Light Source modules combining Sivers' high-power InP DFB lasers with POET's Optical Interposer platform. The deal was more than a supplier agreement: it contractually anchored Sivers' position in a specific CPO architecture at the moment CPO was becoming a central topic in AI infrastructure planning.

Vathulya framed the rationale directly:

> "We see a highly complementary fit between our high-performance DFB lasers and POET's innovative optical interposer platform."

Analyst Tim Savageaux had placed the ELS market opportunity at over $1 billion annually. The POET deal made Sivers the referenced laser supplier for one of the higher-profile bets in that space. When Ayar Labs' SuperNova — a multi-wavelength light source that uses Sivers laser arrays, jointly demonstrated at ECOC 2022 — gained traction in specialist AI infrastructure publications, the Sivers name travelled with it. The stock accelerated through Q4 2025 and into the new year. The pipeline closed the year at $453 million, up 64% year-on-year.

## February 26, 2026: The preliminary read

The Q4 2025 preliminary results, published 26 February, offered incremental validation without a headline breakout. Fourth-quarter net sales reached SEK 80.7 million, up just 5% year-on-year on a reported basis — but up 17% at constant currency, a gap that reflects SEK appreciation rather than operational weakness. Product revenue grew 13% quarter-on-quarter to SEK 21.3 million. Full-year 2025 net sales under K3 came to SEK 304.1 million; the operating loss was SEK 141.3 million.

Two weeks later, the company disclosed a $17 million financing package combining a term loan and convertible debt — a reminder that at SEK 43.5 million of year-end cash, the runway was measured in months, not years.

## May 13, 2026: The restatement that didn't crater anything

The annual report, published 13 May 2026, was the most consequential document in the sequence. It carried PCAOB-aligned restated financials — a prerequisite for a planned US dual listing — and the revisions were not cosmetic. The FY2025 EBIT loss widened by SEK 36 million, from SEK 141.3 million to SEK 177.8 million. Net loss moved from SEK 186.5 million to SEK 222.6 million; EPS fell from SEK -0.69 to SEK -0.81. Restatement drivers included revenue reallocation between periods, revised inventory valuations, updated share-based compensation fair values, and impairment of previously capitalised development expenditure.

| Period | Revenue (SEK M) | EBIT (SEK M) | Net loss (SEK M) |
|---|---|---|---|
| FY2024 (K3 as reported) | 243.7 | n/d | -116.3 |
| FY2024 (PCAOB restated) | 219.2 | n/d | -183.9 |
| FY2025 (K3 as reported) | 304.1 | -141.3 | -186.5 |
| FY2025 (PCAOB restated) | 306.6 | -177.8 | -222.6 |

The stock barely moved. That non-reaction is itself a data point about who now holds the shares. Institutional readers with experience of PCAOB-conversion exercises interpreted the restatement as accounting plumbing ahead of an SEC process — not operational deterioration. The restatement simultaneously reduced FY2024 revenue by SEK 24.5 million and widened the 2024 net loss by SEK 67.6 million, erasing what had looked like a more modest prior-year result. Revenue growth from 2024 to 2025 looks better under the restated figures: SEK 219.2 million to SEK 306.6 million, a 40% increase.

Six days later, a $6.6 million Year 2 grant arrived from the US Department of Defense's Microelectronics Commons program — non-dilutive capital that doubles as a sovereignty-of-supply endorsement timed precisely as the company readied its US listing case.

## The MSCI trigger and the test ahead

Sivers joins the MSCI Sweden Small Cap Index effective 29 May 2026 — the same date Q1 2026 results are scheduled (delayed from an earlier target). Passive funds tracking the index must buy shares regardless of what those results contain. The simultaneity is either fortuitous or a reminder that corporate calendars are never entirely accidental.

The rally has been built on genuine operational improvement — FCF cut from -SEK 151 million to -SEK 66 million over three years, revenue compounding at 36.7% annually since 2016, a pipeline that has grown 16-fold over a decade. But what is not yet real, in any material shipped-and-invoiced sense, is co-packaged optics revenue. The POET ELS modules remain in early prototype phase, with production readiness targeted for end-2026. The unnamed automotive LiDAR customer, whose eight-to-ten year lifecycle value is estimated at $53–138 million, has a production ramp planned for Q4 2026 — still ahead. At SEK 72.90, one detailed bull-case model implies a 2030 fair value closer to SEK 14.52, suggesting the market is pricing a substantially more aggressive ramp and higher terminal margins than even optimistic projections support. The next two to three quarters need to convert that $453 million pipeline into production-stage revenue — not further partnership announcements. The thesis is coherent. The factory has not yet been asked to prove it.
